text.en: A long time ago, Deba and Deep took their family's cows out to graze every day. One day Deba asked how they could be sure no cow was lost, but they did not know how to count. A friend told them to make a mark on the wall for each cow that left, and strike out a mark for each cow that came back. This chapter is about counting, names and grouping things.

Deba and Deep made one mark on the wall for each cow that left the gate. When the cows came home, they struck out one mark for each cow that entered. When all marks are struck out, every cow has come home. If two marks are left, two cows are still missing, so they went to search for them and found them in a field. Tally marks keep track of a count without using number names. We can match one mark with one cow. This idea is called one-to-one matching. We can use marks to keep track of different things, such as 36 cows and 23 sheep, by making separate rows of marks.
Names are made of letters, and we can count the letters in a name. In a game, the animal with the longest name, the one with the most letters, is the captain of the first team, and the one with the shortest name is the captain of the second team. Among tiger, snake, dog, lion, goat, elephant, ox, deer, monkey and rat, the longest name is elephant with 8 letters, and the shortest name is ox with 2 letters. Numbers have names too. 43 is forty-three, and the number name has 10 letters, 5 in forty and 5 in three. 17 is seventeen, and its number name has 9 letters. 56 is fifty-six, and it has 8 letters. Other numbers between 1 and 99 that also have 8 letters are 13, 14, 18, 19, 41, 42, 46, 51, 52, 61, 62 and 66. Among the numbers from 1 to 99, the longest names are seventy-three, seventy-seven and seventy-eight, with 12 letters each. The shortest names are one, two, six and ten, with 3 letters each.
We can group things in different ways. The animal cards can be grouped as those that eat food and those that do not, or by the number of legs. There is more than one correct way to group. Every object must belong to exactly one group. Household things can be grouped as things that need electricity, such as a TV, lamp, fan and clock, and things that do not, such as a chair, bed, pillow and blanket. A group can be made by looking at what is common, such as having four legs, being a thing in the kitchen, or beginning with the same letter.
We can collect information about our class. We can count how many children have the same starting letter in their names, or the same ending letter. We can look at hair styles. Some children have two ponytails, some have one plait and some have short hair. We count each kind and write the numbers. The most common starting letter is the one with the most names. Names of places can be long. Venkatanarasimharajuvaripeta in Andhra Pradesh is a place in India with a very long name.
Deba and Deep had only a few cows at first, so they made one mark on the wall for each cow that left the gate. Later they had many more cows, so the wall had many marks, and at night two marks were still left, so two cows were missing. Their friend Hemant had 36 cows and 23 sheep, so he can make 36 marks for cows in one row and 23 marks for sheep in another row. In class, you can use the same idea to keep track of children who enter and leave the room.
The captain of the first team is the animal with the most letters in its name, which is elephant with 8 letters. The captain of the second team has the fewest letters, which is ox with 2 letters. Mahesh and Kartik can compare names by counting letters, and the longer name is the one with more letters. Let us write the names of five friends, tick the longest name and cross the shortest name.
Write the starting letter of your own name and count how many friends have the same starting letter. Find which starting letter is used most, and which letters are not the starting letter of any name. Count the names that have the same ending letter as yours too.
Teji made her roll number 43 with cards, forty and three, and Jojo made 17 with seventeen. Write your own roll number with number cards and count the letters in its name. Fifty-six has 8 letters, and we can look for other numbers with 8 letters and see what they have in common. The place with the longest name is Venkatanarasimharajuvaripeta, while Ib in Odisha and Od in Gujarat have the shortest names.

problem.en: Deba and Deep made 7 marks when 7 cows left. Five marks were struck out when the cows came back. How many cows are still out?

text.en: Each mark stands for one cow.
Marks left = 7 - 5 = 2.
Two cows are still out.

why.en: They went to search for them.

problem.en: How many letters are in forty-three?

text.en: Forty has 5 letters: f, o, r, t, y.
Three has 5 letters: t, h, r, e, e.
5 + 5 = 10 letters.

problem.en: Group these things: TV, chair, fan, bed. Use the idea of electricity.

text.en: TV and fan need electricity.
Chair and bed do not need electricity.
Two groups: needs electricity and does not.

why.en: Every object is in one group.

problem.en: Count the letters in the number name twenty-five.

text.en: Write the number name: twenty-five.

why.en: We need the name before we can count.

text.en: Twenty has 6 letters and five has 4 letters.
6 + 4 = 10, so twenty-five has 10 letters.

why.en: Add the parts to get the total.

prompt.en: Explain how Deba and Deep made sure every cow came back.

requiredIdeas.en: A mark for each cow leaving
Strike out a mark for each cow returning

commonMisconceptions.en: They needed to count every cow aloud

points.en: We can count by making one mark for each thing, called one-to-one matching.
Names have letters and numbers have names, and we can count the letters.
Things can be grouped in more than one way.
Every object must be in exactly one group.
We can collect information about our class and count it.
The longest name has the most letters and the shortest name has the fewest letters.
